notes: Verified agricultural knowledge base. Recommendations are only triggered when model confidence >= threshold. Do NOT allow the neural network to generate treatment text.
regulatory_notice: All pesticide/fungicide recommendations are general guidelines only. Consult local agricultural extension services for approved products and dosages in your region.

healthy.message: The leaf appears healthy. Continue regular monitoring.
prevention: Maintain optimal plant spacing for air circulation

tomato_early_blight.symptoms: Circular brown lesions with concentric rings, often starting on older lower leaves. Lesions may have yellow halo.
control: Remove and destroy severely infected leaves immediately
Improve air circulation between plants
Apply locally approved copper-based fungicide according to label
Avoid overhead irrigation — water at base of plants
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds or resistant varieties
Maintain soil mulch to reduce soil-splash infection
Avoid working in the field when foliage is wet
tomato_early_blight.regulatory_note: Consult local agriculture extension office for registered fungicides in your region.

tomato_late_blight.symptoms: Irregular water-soaked lesions on leaves that turn brown/black. White sporulation on underside of leaves in humid conditions.
control: Remove and destroy infected plant material immediately
Do not compost infected material
Apply protective fungicide before symptoms appear in high-risk conditions
Consult local recommendations for mancozeb or copper-based protectants
prevention: Avoid cool wet conditions (above 90% humidity with 10–15°C)
Monitor field regularly during rainy seasons
tomato_late_blight.regulatory_note: Late blight spreads rapidly. Seek professional field diagnosis to confirm before applying systemic fungicides.

tomato_leaf_mold.symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaf surface with olive-green to gray mold growth on underside.
control: Remove affected leaves
Improve greenhouse ventilation if growing under cover
Apply locally registered fungicide for leaf mold
tomato_leaf_mold.regulatory_note: Primarily affects greenhouse tomatoes. Consult extension services for field management.

tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark border and lighter center. Tiny black fruiting bodies visible inside spots.
control: Remove infected leaves promptly
Avoid working in wet field conditions
Apply copper or chlorothalonil fungicide (where registered)
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.regulatory_note: Check local regulations before applying synthetic fungicides.

tomato_target_spot.symptoms: Concentric ring pattern forming target-like spots. Brown lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit.
control: Apply registered fungicide at first sign of disease
Remove and destroy infected plant debris

tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mosaic pattern of light and dark green patches on leaves. Leaf distortion, curling, and stunted growth.
control: No chemical cure for viral diseases
Remove and destroy infected plants
Control aphid and whitefly vectors
Disinfect tools between plants
prevention: Use virus-indexed seeds or certified transplants
Wash hands thoroughly before handling plants
Do not smoke near tomato plants (tobacco mosaic risk)
tomato_mosaic_virus.regulatory_note: Viral diseases cannot be treated chemically. Focus on prevention and vector control.

rice_brown_spot.symptoms: Oval to circular brown lesions with yellow halo. Severe infection causes premature leaf death.
control: Apply fungicide at early infection stage (consult local recommendations)
Ensure balanced silicon and potassium nutrition
prevention: Maintain optimal soil nutrition — brown spot is often linked to nutrient stress
rice_brown_spot.regulatory_note: Linked to nutrient deficiency. Soil testing recommended before treatment.

rice_leaf_blast.symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with gray-white center and brown border. Severe cases lead to leaf death.
control: Apply locally approved fungicide at early tillering and heading stages
Avoid excessive nitrogen application
prevention: Monitor weather conditions — blast is favored by cool wet nights
rice_leaf_blast.regulatory_note: Tricyclazole and propiconazole are commonly used where registered — check local approvals.

powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaf surface. Leaves may curl and distort under heavy infection.
control: Apply sulfur-based or registered fungicide
Remove heavily infected leaves

pest_damage_unspecified.message: Signs of pest activity are visible but the specific pest cannot be reliably identified from this image.
control: Inspect the leaf underside carefully for insects, eggs, or webbing
Capture a close-up image of visible insects for identification
Consult local agricultural extension for pest identification before treatment
prevention: Monitor for early signs of pest activity

physical_damage_unspecified.message: Mechanical or physical damage to leaf tissue is visible.
control: Monitor for secondary fungal infection at damaged sites
Remove severely damaged leaves to reduce infection risk
prevention: Handle plants carefully during field operations

unknown.message: The leaf condition could not be reliably identified from this image.
unknown.guidance: Please capture a closer, well-lit image of the affected leaf, or consult a local agricultural expert for in-person diagnosis.

low_confidence.message: Analysis confidence is insufficient for a reliable diagnosis.
low_confidence.guidance: Please capture a clearer image in good lighting with the leaf filling most of the frame. If the issue persists, consult an agricultural expert.
